description:
Château de la Rozelle is an elegant residence built in 1830 in the Loire Valley, near Cellettes. It is a single-building estate that has been expanded over the years to its current 22-room configuration while remaining one continuous structure.

Today all 22 air-conditioned rooms are within this single building.

The château's 1830 construction date places it among the 19th-century country houses of the Loire Valley, built as elegant residences rather than medieval fortresses, a common pattern for many properties carrying the "château" name in the region.

The estate's expansion over the years into its current 22-room form, while remaining a single continuous structure, distinguishes la Rozelle from properties that added separate annex buildings to grow their room count.

The château's position in Cellettes, within easy reach of both Château de Chambord and Château de Cheverny, gives guests staying here a convenient base for exploring two of the Loire Valley's most visited châteaux.

faqs.question: Is Château de la Rozelle a medieval fortress?
faqs.answer: No — it is a 19th-century residence, built in 1830, typical of the many Loire Valley "châteaux" built as elegant country houses rather than defensive fortresses.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms at Château de la Rozelle within one building?
faqs.answer: Yes — all 22 rooms are within the single 1830 château, expanded over the years while remaining one continuous structure.

faqs.question: What other châteaux are near Château de la Rozelle?
faqs.answer: Château de Chambord and Château de Cheverny are both a short drive away.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** In Cellettes, Loir-et-Cher, in the Loire Valley.

**Rooms & rates:** 22 rooms from about €140 per night, all within the 1830 château building.

**On-site:** Garden grounds, breakfast service, air-conditioned rooms throughout.

**Good to know:** A 19th-century (not medieval) château — an elegant single-building residence rather than a fortress, typical of many Loire Valley "châteaux" built as country houses.

**Combine with:** Château de Chambord and Château de Cheverny, both a short drive away in the Loire Valley.
